title: Correspondent Bank Charges Passed On with Payout Methods Return Charges
content:
When a transfer to a Payout Methods method comes back, the correspondent bank's handling of the returned funds is passed on in the return charge according to the size of the return. The size is the returned amount: the amount that the latest return on the method booked back to the method.

## Charge passed on, by size of the return

| Returned amount | Correspondent charge passed on |
|---|---|
| USD 5000.00 or more | A lifting charge of 0.10 percent of the returned amount |
| USD 1000.00 or more, and below USD 5000.00 | A flat correspondent charge of USD 6.00 |
| Below USD 1000.00 | No correspondent charge |

The lifting charge is the returned amount multiplied by 0.10 and divided by one hundred, carried unrounded.

## Both sides of each line (hypothetical returns)

| Returned amount | Correspondent charge |
|---|---|
| USD 12000.00 | 0.10 percent: USD 12.00 |
| USD 5000.00 | 0.10 percent: USD 5.00 |
| USD 4999.99 | Flat USD 6.00 |
| USD 1000.00 | Flat USD 6.00 |
| USD 999.99 | None |
| USD 7333.33 | 0.10 percent: USD 7.33333, carried unrounded |

## Treasury notes

- The lifting charge and the flat charge never apply together: a return of USD 5000.00 or more carries the percentage lifting charge only.
- The returned amount is the amount booked back by the latest return on the method, the return the charge names; earlier returns to the method do not add to it.
